newsitem.title: USA: Bethlehem Steel sets $375 mln Q4 charge.
newsitem.headline: Bethlehem Steel sets $375 mln Q4 charge.

text.p: Bethlehem Steel Corp said Wednesday directors had approved a restructuring plan that will result in a fourth-quarter, after-tax charge of about $375 million.

Designed "to improve financial performance and stockholder value," the plan calls for the sale of Bethlehem Structural Products Corp's Structural Mill, BethForge Inc, CENTEC Roll Corp and BethShip Inc's Sparrows Point Yard, the company said.
In addition, the Coke Division at Bethlehem, Pa., will be written off as an impaired asset, it said.
The four divisions to be sold will continue to be operated while buyers are sought. "It is hoped that the businesses will continue to be operated under new ownership," it said.

"If they cannot be sold in a scheduled period of time, they will be shut down in an orderly manner and efforts to sell the businesses in total or as individual assets will continue," the company said. It did not specify what the "scheduled period" was.
"These businesses, which comprise less than 10 percent of our total revenues, have continued to be unprofitable," Bethlehem said.
The divisions to be sold employ 2,235 workers, Bethlehem spokesman Art Roth said. More than 90 percent of these employees are eligible for pension benefits, the company said.
"The decisions announced today will enhance our future performance," Chief Executive Curtis Barnette said.

"With this decision now behind us, we will intensify our efforts to improve the competitiveness of our core steel operations at our Burns Harbor and Sparrows Point Divisions and at Pennsylvania Steel Technologies Inc."
He said implementation of the plan would include four principal areas of focus and responsibility.
"First, these Divisions will be operated for a period of time while efforts to sell them are being made."

"Second, Bethlehem will begin an immediate effort to sell these businesses. This effort will be headed by Gary L. Millenbruch, Bethlehem's executive vice president, chief financial officer and treasurer."
Millenbruch will work with financial advisors, United Steelworkers union representatives and others, Barnette said.
Third, employee benefits, training and outplacement will be provided to all affected employees under the responsibility of Dorothy Stephenson, Bethlehem's vice president, human resources.
Fourth, the development of Bethlehem's properties on the south side of Bethlehem, Pa., will continue.

Located in Bethlehem, Pa., Bethlehem Structural Products produces structural steel shapes and piling for the construction market. Its principal operating facilities include a 40-inch blooming mill and a 44-inch combination rolling mill. It employs about 900 workers.

Bethlehem noted that in the fourth quarter of 1995 it discontinued iron and steelmaking operations at Bethlehem Structural and upgraded the 44-inch rolling mill in an effort to reduce costs and improve performance. This structural mill currently obtains its semi-finished steel requirements from Bethlehem's Pennsylvania Steel Technologies and the Sparrows Point Division, as well as from outside suppliers.

The Bethlehem Coke Division, which operates two coke oven batteries Structural Products site, will continue to produce coke for Bethlehem's Sparrows Point and Burns Harbor Divisions, and for trade customers.
It employs about 600 people.

BethForge, located in Bethlehem, manufactures and fabricates forged steel products for the metalworking, electrical power generating and nuclear industries from steel ingots produced at Pennsylvania Steel Technologies. It employs about 500 people.
Also located in Bethlehem, CENTEC produces centrifugally cast rolls for the metal working industry. It employs about 135 workers.
BethShip operates a ship repair yard at Sparrows Point, Md., on Baltimore Harbor, which repairs and services ships and fabricates industrial products. It employs about 700 workers.
